# Marilla Cuthbert

[Aid Society](../codex/factions.md#aid-society)

## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman characterized by her angular, curveless frame and sallow cheeks. Her dark hair, which she wears tightly twisted into a hard little knot at the back, shows gray streaks that have grown grayer over time.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation P11](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0011), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015)_

## Personality

A practical, sensible, and self-contained woman, Marilla possesses a rigid conscience and narrow experience, firmly disbelieving in imagining things to be different from reality. Characterized by an unsympathetic nature, she is strict and critical, being particularly fond of tacking a moral onto every remark made to a child. In line with her principles, she consistently refuses to criticize ministers, though she is inclined to become sarcastic when recovering from headaches. Despite being inexorable when setting disciplinary lessons, she has notably mellowed over time. She views it as her duty to drill [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, and she is locally celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

## History

When [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) went to collect an orphan boy to help on their farm, Marilla Cuthbert explained the plan to her neighbor Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), but was shocked when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) instead brought home a girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md). Though Marilla initially insisted on sending [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back, she changed her mind after learning about Anne's tragic childhood and deciding not to hand her over to a harsh local woman. Taking responsibility for Anne's upbringing, Marilla began instructing her in neatness and religion, but was soon forced to send [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to her room after the girl flew into a rage over Rachel's blunt insults. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) apologized and was permitted to stay, Marilla gradually developed a deep, warm affection for her, though she continued to strictly manage her. Marilla made plain clothes for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), scolded her for decorating her hat with wild flowers for church, and sent her into a dark spruce grove to cure her of dramatic fears about ghosts. Over the following years, Marilla supported Anne's growth, allowing her to attend a Sunday school picnic after realizing she had wrongly accused [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) of losing a missing brooch, and agreeing to let [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) join an advanced class to prepare for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). During Anne's broken ankle recovery, Marilla came to recognize how deeply she cared for the girl. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) died suddenly following news of a bank failure, Marilla wept alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and opened up about a past youthful romance with John Blythe. Soon after, an oculist warned Marilla that she faced total blindness unless she gave up heavy eye work, leading [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to forfeit her scholarship to remain at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and care for her.

## Quotes

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

> "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P4](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0004)

> "and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022)

> “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just. “If you put that brooch back it’s there still. If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”

> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P9](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0009)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla becomes Anne's adoptive mother and dear friend, initially accepting the orphan girl at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) after a mix-up where she and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) had expected a boy. Though Marilla focuses on disciplining Anne's lack of religious training and theatrical outbursts, she refuses to give [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) away to a harsh neighbor and grows deeply affectionate toward her.

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

[Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) is Marilla's neighbor and friend, frequently visiting [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for tea and offering advice on household and child-rearing matters. While [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) occasionally causes friction—such as driving [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) into a rage with her blunt comments or voicing strong warnings about adoption—Marilla trusts her counsel, consulting her on Anne's upbringing and traveling together to political meetings.
